findings.description:
In format_message (lines 174 and 176 of bin/fm-pr-comments-poll.sh), `loc` is built with `"
Location: $path"` and `"$loc
Review state: $state"`. Bash does NOT interpret 
 as a newline in double-quoted strings — it is a literal backslash-n. When $loc is expanded inside the heredoc at line 182 (`URL: $url$loc`), the injected message reads `URL: https://…
Location: src/file.ts:42` all on one line. The content is present, just crammed on one line. The test passes because `grep -F "Location: src/map.ts:43"` matches it as a substring of that garbled line, so the test does not catch this. Fix: use `$'
'` for each newline: `loc=$'
'"Location: $path"` and `loc="$loc"$'
'"Review state: $state"`.

json_lines_for_pr (lines 130–138 of bin/fm-pr-comments-poll.sh) runs three sequential `gh api` calls without `set -e`. Each failure writes to stderr but does not abort the function, so a failure on the issue-comments or review-comments call silently emits partial output. The exit-code check at line 214 (`if ! json_lines_for_pr … > $events 2>$events.err`) only sees the exit code of the final (reviews) call. If the first two calls fail but the third succeeds, no error is emitted and the affected events are silently dropped until the next poll. Fix: accumulate exit codes across all three calls and return non-zero if any failed.

In process_task (line 248 of bin/fm-pr-comments-poll.sh), the `else` branch on send failure assigns `rc=0`, which is a no-op since `rc` was already 0. This looks like a copy-paste artifact from an earlier version that intended `rc=1` to propagate the failure to the caller. The main loop (`selected_tasks | while … do process_task "$id"; done`) ignores the return code anyway, so there is no functional impact. The error is still surfaced through emit_error_once. Either remove the dead assignment or make it `rc=1` for clarity.

write_check in bin/fm-pr-comments.sh (line 52) embeds $FM_ROOT, $FM_HOME, and $STATE into the generated check shim as bare unquoted default values inside `${VAR:-path}` expansions. A path containing a space, `}`, or `$` would break the generated script at shell parse time. In practice firstmate homes do not use such paths, but the shim is not robust against unusual setups.

tool_input.risk_rationale: The change is purely additive — new scripts and docs only, no modifications to existing watcher, wake, or lifecycle infrastructure — and the bugs found are cosmetic (literal \\n) or low-consequence partial-failure gaps in an already error-tolerant design.
tool_input.testing_summary: Three smoke tests cover the main flows: prime-then-dedupe for issue comments, review comment delivery with file/line context and bot filtering, and disable cleaning the check shim. The \\n formatting bug is masked in the test because `grep -F` matches it as a substring regardless of newlines. No tests for the partial-failure scenario in json_lines_for_pr.
tested: enable primes existing comments without sending them
second poll does not inject duplicates
bot comments are ignored and marked seen
review comments include file and line context
disable all removes the check shim
